about: Active travel alerts for an Indian passport holder: airline suspensions, Indian embassy or MEA advisories, entry restrictions and closures. An alert stays listed until it is lifted. sourceLevel is official (official page read) or news (reported by news, official page not read yet).

alerts.title: Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa Air Saudi flight suspensions
alerts.summary: IndiGo announced on 18 November 2026 that all flights to and from Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh and Dammam are cancelled until 30 November inclusive. Akasa Air announced on 12 November that all Riyadh and Jeddah flights are suspended until 30 November inclusive; affected passengers can request a full refund or reschedule at no additional cost. Air India announced on 20 November that its flights and Air India Express flights to and from Jeddah are suspended until 24 November, while Riyadh and Dammam remain suspended until 30 November. Passengers with confirmed Jeddah bookings made on or before 20 November for travel up to 24 November can reschedule without charge subject to availability or cancel for a full refund. The same options apply to confirmed Riyadh and Dammam bookings made on or before 10 November for travel up to 30 November. Air India passengers may rebook through an operating Air India station in Saudi Arabia; Air India Express passengers may rebook through an operating Air India Express station in Saudi Arabia or Bahrain. Revised travel can be completed by 8 December for Jeddah bookings, or 14 December for Riyadh and Dammam bookings.

alerts.title: Indian Embassy in Riyadh safety advisory
alerts.summary: The Indian Embassy in Riyadh asked Indians in Saudi Arabia to take precautions against possible aerial attacks, stay indoors during attacks and follow local authorities. Travellers, including Umrah pilgrims, should expect airport disruption and cancelled flights that could extend a stay. Saudi authorities have said visitors who overstay because no flights are available can leave without fines.

alerts.title: China visa applications now go to the embassy or consulate, from 26 October 2026
alerts.summary: The Chinese Embassy in New Delhi and the Consulate General in Mumbai now take visa applications directly. Apply online first at consular.mfa.gov.cn/VISA, then submit your passport and documents in person within 30 days of the approval email. Residents of Maharashtra and Karnataka apply through Mumbai. Residents of Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal apply through the Embassy in New Delhi for now. Everyone else applies through the Embassy in New Delhi. Fingerprints are waived until 31 December 2026 for short-term visas of up to 180 days. Processing takes 7 working days, or 4 with express service. Fees for Indian passport holders start at Rs 2,900 for a single entry. Fees are paid when you collect the visa.

alerts.title: Australian visa applicants in India may need to give biometrics, from 26 October 2026
alerts.summary: From 26 October 2026, applicants for an Australian visa in India may be required to provide biometrics, including fingerprints and a facial image. Australia is expanding this to nearly 60 countries, including India. The Department of Home Affairs will tell you if you must provide biometrics and how to do it. Depending on your case, you may be asked to attend an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre in person, or to provide biometrics digitally through the Australian Immi App. If you gave biometrics at a centre before and hold a valid passport, you may be able to use the app at no cost. It applies only to new applications lodged from 26 October 2026 and does not affect applications already submitted. Processing times are not expected to change if you complete the biometrics promptly.

alerts.title: New ID document rule for Indians travelling to or from Nepal
alerts.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs published an amendment to the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025 in the Gazette of India on 5 November 2026 (S.O. 6027(E), dated 4 November). An Indian citizen entering India from Nepal or leaving India for Nepal by land or air must show the immigration officer one of the documents specified in the Visa Manual to establish identity, and give any information the officer asks for. The passport and visa exemption does not cover an Indian citizen travelling to or from any country other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border, by land or air. In that case a valid passport is required and entry or exit must be through a designated immigration post. The order does not list the accepted documents. They are in the Visa Manual, which has not been read here, so check the exact list before you travel.

alerts.title: India advises avoiding non-essential travel to the DR Congo (Ebola)
alerts.summary: The Government of India Health Ministry advisory dated 23 May 2026, posted on the Indian embassy in Kinshasa website, advises all Indian citizens to avoid non-essential travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda and South Sudan because of the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak, which WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May 2026. CDC lists Ituri and North Kivu as Level 4 (avoid all travel).

alerts.title: Malaysia ends visa-free entry for Indians from 1 January 2027
alerts.summary: The Immigration Department of Malaysia announced on 17 November 2026 that Indian nationals entering Malaysia from 1 January 2027 must obtain a valid visa before arrival. Applications through the MyVISA portal open on 1 December 2026. Visa processing fees are non-refundable, including after a refusal, policy change or change of travel plans. The current exemption for visits of up to 30 days runs until 31 December 2026. The department says entry requirements may change under Malaysian government directives.

alerts.title: Pakistan extends airspace ban on Indian aircraft until 24 December 2026
alerts.summary: The Pakistan Airports Authority announced on 19 November 2026 that the ban on Indian-registered aircraft and aircraft owned, operated or leased by Indian airlines or operators, including military flights, is extended until 24 December 2026 at 04:59 AM. The restriction remains in force across Pakistani airspace. The announcement does not specify the time zone.

alerts.title: Bangladesh visa centres run by DU Digital in Kolkata and Siliguri close after 30 November
alerts.summary: The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata announced on 17 November 2026 that its visa outsourcing contract with DU Digital Global Ltd ends on 30 November 2026 and will not be renewed. The Bangladesh visa application centres operated by DU Digital in Kolkata and Siliguri will stop operating at their current addresses after that date. The notice asks applicants not to submit visa applications at those centres after 30 November. The name and address of the new visa application centre will be announced in a separate notice.

alerts.title: Indian Embassy advises postponing all travel to Iran
alerts.summary: The Embassy of India in Tehran advised on 19 July 2026 that Indian nationals intending to travel to Iran for any purpose should postpone travel until the security environment improves. Indians already in Iran should consider temporarily exiting using available flights. Those remaining should exercise the highest possible caution, avoid locations with increased military activity such as the southern coast, follow local authorities and register with the Embassy. The advisory remains displayed prominently on the Embassy website.

alerts.title: Some areas and tourism facilities remain under repair after Hurricane Melissa
alerts.summary: As checked on 22 November 2026, Jamaica Tourist Board says Jamaica is open to visitors, with most resort areas operating, but some areas remain under repair and utilities are still being restored in some resort areas. All three international airports have resumed full operations and seaports are open. The board asks visitors to confirm that their booked accommodation can host them and to check hotel operating status. It also advises avoiding floodwater because of health risks.

alerts.title: QazETA phased rollout; mandatory from 1 July 2027
alerts.summary: Kazakhstan MFA says the free QazETA rollout started at Aktau airport and selected road checkpoints on 1 November 2026, expands to Astana and Almaty airports on 1 January 2027 and all remaining checkpoints on 1 March 2027. It becomes mandatory from 1 July 2027. Until then, absence of an ETA alone is not grounds for refusing entry. Apply at least 72 hours before travel. The authorisation is valid for 180 days and does not extend the visa-free stay.

alerts.title: Prescribed inbound travel health insurance required for Kenya visitors
alerts.summary: The Indian High Commission in Nairobi says non-exempt foreign visitors entering Kenya from 5 October 2026 for stays under 12 months must obtain prescribed inbound travel health insurance before arrival, regardless of when their eTA or tickets were issued. Each visitor, including minors, needs individual coverage. Buy through the official eTA portal, or insurance.ecitizen.go.ke if already holding an eTA. Foreign travel or medical insurance is not a substitute. The policy is valid for 90 days and multiple entries while coverage remains valid. Airlines and immigration may verify it. Transit passengers who do not seek entry are exempt.

alerts.title: CDC reports Ebola Bundibugyo cases in Nairobi
alerts.summary: CDC reports an imported case and other linked cases of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Nairobi. Its Level 1 notice recommends usual precautions, including avoiding contact with symptomatic people or their body fluids. Travellers who develop symptoms should isolate, not travel, and contact local health authorities or a healthcare facility before attending. No vaccines or specific treatments are approved for this disease.

alerts.title: Ireland short-stay visa waiver continues until 31 December 2026
alerts.summary: Irish Immigration Service Delivery confirms that the Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme continues until 31 December 2026 and may be amended at any time. Eligible Indian passport holders who are not living long term in the UK can travel to Ireland without a separate Irish visa after lawfully entering the UK on a qualifying short-stay visit or business visa. The intended Irish visit must end before their current UK immigration permission expires. The maximum stay is 90 days or the remaining UK permission, whichever is shorter, and an Irish immigration officer decides whether to admit the traveller and for how long. UK transit visas and visas for marriage or civil partnership visits do not qualify. An unused UK visa or airside transit through the UK is not sufficient. This programme is separate from the British Irish Visa Scheme.

alerts.title: Revised Kyrgyz visa procedure and tourist category
alerts.summary: The Indian Embassy reports that Decree No. 312 of 30 April 2026 revised Kyrgyz visa procedures and expanded visa categories. The official e-visa portal lists Tourist visa TS with validity up to 30 calendar days and Transit visa TR with validity up to 3 calendar days. Tourist and transit visas are not issued to foreigners already staying in Kyrgyzstan, including under a visa-free regime. The Embassy asks Indian visitors for tourism, business and work to follow the revised rules.

alerts.title: Digital immigration form required for entry and departure
alerts.summary: The Indian Embassy states that foreign passport holders must register the Lao Digital Immigration Form within 3 days before entering or departing Laos. The notice says the form applies at all international checkpoints from the beginning of 2026. Registration is through the official Lao immigration website and does not replace a visa.

alerts.title: 48-hour travel declaration for holders of other Schengen visas
alerts.summary: Indian passport holders entering Latvia without a visa or residence permit issued by Latvia must submit the Electronic Travel Declaration at eta.gov.lv at least 48 hours before arrival, including transit across Latvia. A valid visa or residence permit from another Schengen country does not exempt an Indian traveller. Latvian visa and residence permit holders are exempt. The declaration does not replace a visa or other entry conditions.
